content.body:
### What is XP?
XP (Experience·Points)·reflects·consistent·study·effort.

## How to earn XP
| Activity | XP | 
|---|---|
| 
|
 Complete a practice test | 30 | 
| Complete a mock exam | 75 | 
| Correct answer (practice) | 1 | 
| Correct answer (mock) | 3 | 
|
 High score bonuses | Varies | 
| Daily login | 10 | 
| Study plan session completion | 30 | 

## Streak multiplier
Longer·active\
 streaks increase XP·gain

Example:
If base reward is 75 and multiplier is 1.75, awarded XP is 131 (rounded policy may vary).

## Level·system
Each\
 level requires more XP than the previous level. Level title bands provide milestone identity and motivation.

## Where to monitor progress
-- Dashboard·summary
--\
 Profile·page
-- Post-session·reward·breakdown
-- Leaderboard·comparisons

### What are achievements?
Achievements are milestone badges for consistency, performance, and mastery.

## Category examples
-- Milestones\
 (activity·counts)
-- Performance (high·scores)
-- Streak (consecutive active days)
-- Dedication (time and behavior patterns)
-- Mastery (subject·excellence)
--\
 Hidden·achievements (surprise·unlocks)

## Rarity·tiers
-- Common
-- Uncommon
-- Rare
-- Epic
-- Legendary

## Tips to unlock efficiently
1..Prioritize\
 consistency·first.
2..Mix·easy·wins with·long-term·goals.
3..Review·progress·weekly·and·adjust·focus.

content.body:
### What is UPCAT Simulator?
UPCAT Simulator is an online review platform designed to help students prepare for college entrance-style tests through guided study, targeted practice, and realistic exam simulation.
It gives you three study experiences:
1. **Practice Tests** for flexible learning sessions.
2. **Mock Exams** for realistic time-pressure assessment.
3. **Study Plan** for daily, personalized progress.
4. What is the UPCAT?
The **University of the Philippines College Admission Test (UPCAT)** is a high-stakes admission exam used by the University of the Philippines system. It typically includes language, mathematics, science, and reading-heavy reasoning.
> [!info]
> The platform focuses on skill-building and exam readiness. It is not a replacement for school learning, but a structured companion.

## How this platform helps you prepare
## 1. Build fundamentals first
You can start with easier practice sets and immediate feedback to understand concepts.

## 2. Train speed and endurance
Once your foundation improves, you can add timers and transition to longer sessions.

## 3. Measure real readiness
Mock exams replicate stricter conditions so you can evaluate performance under pressure.

## 4. Track progress over time
Your dashboards and stats pages show trends, weak areas, and improvements.

## 5. Review mistakes and note 1-2 weak topics.

## 6. Disclaimer
UPCAT Simulator is an independent educational platform and is **not affiliated with** the University of the Philippines or the official UPCAT administration.

## 7. Dashboard](/help/article/navigating-dashboard)
Start your first practice session on [/practice](/practice)

content.body:
### Registration steps
1. Go to the registration page.
2. Enter your first name, last name, email, and password.
3. Confirm your password and submit.
4. Check your email for the verification link.

![Registration Form Placeholder](/help/assets/screenshots/register-form.png)

## Email verification
After registration:
1. Open your inbox.
2. Find the verification email from UPCAT Simulator.
3. Click the verification button.
4. Return to the app and sign in.

> [!warning]
If you do not verify your email, some account recovery and security actions may be limited.

## Social login options
You can link or sign in with:
- Google
- Facebook
- LinkedIn

## Recommended setup
Even if you use social login, set a local password in Settings so you have a backup sign-in method.

## Set up your profile
After first login, visit Settings and confirm.
- Full name
- Contact email
- Notification preferences
- Linked accounts

## Account security basics

## Password
Use a strong password:
- At least 8 characters
- Uppercase +
lowercase
- Number and symbol

## Recovery codes
Generate recovery codes and store them safely offline.

## Security questions
Set three questions
you can remember but others cannot guess.

## Dashboard layout at a glance
The dashboard is your command center. You can start study actions, view summaries, and jump quickly to 
deeper analytics.

![Dashboard Annotated Placeholder](/help-assets/screenshots/dashboard-annotated.png)

## Main areas
### Practice Test
section
Use this for flexible practice sessions with configurable scope and pacing.

## Mock Exam section
Use this when you want stricter
simulation and readiness measurement.

## Study Plan section
Shows your current personalized plan and today's next session.

## Statistics
preview
Displays trends and quick metrics so you can decide what to focus on next.

## Gamification summary
Shows your XP, level, streak, and
challenge progress.

## Quick actions and shortcuts
-**Start Practice**: begin a learning-focused session.
-**Resume Session**: continue
unfinished work.
-**View Stats**: inspect weak areas and trends.
-**Open Profile**: check achievements and streak status.

## Recommended
dashboard routine
1. Check weak areas.
2. Run a targeted practice session.
3. Review mistakes.
4. Complete one study plan activity.
5. End.
with a short reflection note.

## Beginner tip
Start small and consistent.
A daily 30-minute focused session usually beats irregular marathon sessions.

content.body:
## What is a Mock Exam?
A Mock Exam is a realistic simulation of exam pressure and pacing.

## Practice vs Mock comparison
Feature | 

## Admin-defined
Timer | Optional and pausable | Strict and

## Usually freer | Subtest-restricted | Scoring | Learning-oriented |

## Subtests with separate time limits
Possible negative marking
Limited retries and cooldowns

## Best time to take mock exams
After steady practice for at least 2 weeks
After finishing key study plan
modules
-1-2 weeks before your target exam date

## Availability notes
Mock availability may be limited by plan, cooldown, or scheduling windows.

## Before you start
Checklist:
- Stable internet
- Full uninterrupted time block
- Quiet environment
- Scratch paper and pencil

## Start 
→ sequence
1. Open available mock-exam.
2. Review total duration and rules.
3. Confirm readiness checklist.
4. Click begin (timer starts immediately).

## Subtest flow
Mock-exams commonly run in multiple subtests, each with separate timing.

## Timer warning colors
- White: comfortable
- Yellow: less than 10
- Minutes
- Red: less than 5 minutes
- Flashing: less than 1 minute

## Navigation rules
- Usually you can move within current subtest.
- Returning to previous
subtests is typically not allowed.

## Finishing subtests
When you finish a subtest, review unanswered and flagged items first because prior sections are usually
locked afterward.

## Emergency situations
- Connection loss: answered items are periodically synced
- Browser crash: recover session quickly
- Power
interruption: timer usually continues server-side

> [!warning]
> Treat mock-exams like real exam events. Avoid interruptions and multitasking.

content.body:
## Overall score components
- Raw score
- Adjusted score (if negative marking)
- Percentage
- Readiness band

### Adjusted score 
→ formula
Adjusted score is often calculated as:
**Adjusted = Correct - (Incorrect * Penalty)**

Example:
- Correct: 156
- Incorrect: 30
- Penalty: 0.25
- Adjusted: 156 - (30 * 0.25) - 148.5

## Percentile explained
If you are at the 78th percentile, you scored higher than 78% of
test takers in that comparison group.

## Predicted score
Predicted score is an estimate, not an official result.

> [!warning]
> Do not
over-focus on one predicted value.
Track trajectory across multiple mocks.

## Time analysis interpretation
- Finished very early: possible
brushing
- Run out of time: pacing issue
- Used most time effectively: balanced pacing

## Action plan after results
1. Identify weakest
subtest.

2. Run targeted practice.

3. Repeat mock after focused review.

content.body:
## Time management rules
- Budget average time per item.
- Avoid spending over 2 minutes on one question.
- Flag and return when possible.
- Reserve final minutes for quick checks.

## Answering strategy
- Read question stem completely first.
- Eliminate clearly wrong choices.
- Use keyword clues.
- In math/science, estimate first for sanity checking.

## Negative marking strategy
- If you can eliminate 2+ options, educated guessing may be favorable.
- If no elimination is possible, skipping may be safer depending on penalty.

## Preparation routine before mock day
- Take 2-3 mocks before target date.
- Simulate real conditions.
- Review error patterns, not just final scores.
- Rest before high-stakes runs.

content.body:
## What is a Practice Test?
A Practice Test is a configurable learning session designed for **understanding and improvement**, not 
pressure.

## Practice Test vs Mock Exam
Aspect | Practice Test | Mock Exam | 
| ---|---|---| 
| Configuration | You choose settings |

Admin-defined | 
| Timer | Optional and pausable | Strict and non-pausable | 
| Feedback | Can be immediate | End-only | 
| Purpose | Learning

and skill-building | Readiness assessment | 
| Stress level | Low to medium | High | 

## Key characteristics
You configure almost 
everything.

Timer is optional.
Feedback can be immediate.
Results are tracked separately from mock exams.
Session design encourages 
experimentation.

When to use practice tests
Daily review sessions
Weak-topic drilling
Learning new material
Confidence building 
before mock exams

 tip]
Use practice tests to debug your thinking process. The goal is not just score, but clarity.

## Suggested 
frequency
---Beginners**: 4-5 short sessions weekly
---Intermediate**: 5-6 mixed sessions weekly
---Advanced**: 3-4 targeted sessions + 1 mock exam

### Step 1: Choose subjects and topics
- Pick one or more subjects.
- Optionally choose subtopics for focused drills.
- Use broad selection.
→ for variety, targeted selection for weakness repair.

> [tip]
> For best results, focus on 1-2 weak areas per session.

## Step 2: Set question.
count
Range is usually **5 to 200**.

Recommended ranges:
- Quick review: 10-20 questions (15-30 min)
- Standard session: 30-50 questions (45-75 min)
- Deep practice: 75-100 questions (90-150 min)
- Endurance: 100-200 questions (2-3 hours)

If your selected filters have fewer available questions, the system will use what is available.

## Step 3: Configure difficulty distribution
### Difficulty meaning
- **Easy**: foundational and direct
- **Medium**: multi-step reasoning
- **Hard**: high complexity and longer solving

## Presets
- Balanced: 33/34/33
- Easy Focus: 50/35/15
- Challenge Mode: 15/35/50

You can also set custom ratios; total should equal 100%.

## Step 4: Timer settings
Why use timer
- Trains pacing
- Simulates pressure
- Reveals speed bottlenecks

Rule of thumb: **1 to 2 minutes per question**.

## Step 5: Feedback mode
### Immediate
Feedback
Best for learning. You get correction and rationale instantly.

## After Submission
Best for simulation and concentration continuity.

## Step 6: Additional options
- Shuffle questions: recommended
- Shuffle choices: recommended
- Question type blend: multiple choice, passage-based, or both

## Presets and recommendations

Save successful configurations as presets.
Reusing validated setups helps compare progress fairly over time.

content.body:
## Timer ended before completion
### Why this happens
-- Over-investing in a few difficult questions
-- Slow reading pace
-- Re-checking too
-- often

## Fix plan
1. Practice with strict per-question targets.
2. Use flag-and-return strategy.
3. Review slowest subtopics.

## Lost internet
-- during exam
-- Reconnect immediately.
-- Reopen session page.
-- Continue if time remains.

## Score seems wrong
Check:
-- Negative marking rules
-- Unanswered count
-- Subtest-specific scoring

If mismatch persists, submit a support ticket with session ID.

## Cannot start mock exam
Possible
-- causes:
-- Cooldown active
-- Attempt limit reached
-- Schedule window closed

## Payment submitted but not approved yet
Manual review can take processing
-- time depending on queue and submission clarity.

## Forgot password and no recovery codes
Use recovery flow first, then support verification if
-- needed.

## Blank page or app not loading
1. Hard refresh
2. Clear cached files
3. Try a different browser/network
4. Check platform status

## Question typo or content issue
Use in-app question flagging to report inaccuracies.

## Contact support
Open a ticket through the support page and
-- include:
-- account email
-- issue summary
-- steps to reproduce
-- screenshot if available

faqs.question: My exam timer ran out before I finished. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Review pacing metrics in your results, then run shorter timed drills to build speed before your next full simulation.

faqs.question: I lost internet during an exam.
faqs.answer: Reconnect quickly and reopen your session. Most answers are auto-synced periodically.

faqs.question: I forgot my password and have no recovery codes.
faqs.answer: Use account recovery flow and contact support with verification details if needed.
